To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the performance of a two layer electrolyte cell can be predicted using the materials properties and cell dimensions, and that the electron blocking characteristics and the ionic conductivities of the materials in contact with the YSZ electrolyte are the most important factors in the design of such a cell.

the open circuit voltage of a double layer electrolyte cell can be increased by the presence of an electron blocking layer, but the oxygen permeability is also reduced; the electron blocking layer thickness has to be carefully chosen, and the electron blocking properties are strongly dependent on the materials properties of the second electrolytic layer.
the performance of double layer cells is strongly dependent on the materials properties of the second electrolytic layer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the evaluation of the performance of two layer double layer electrolyte (DLE) cells, including one electron blocking layer (EBL).
the development of a new generation of oxygen separation devices based on the use of two electrolyte layers.
the development of a fundamental understanding of double layer electrolytes for oxygen separation applications.

the performance of double layer cells is a function of the materials electrical properties, and the relative layer thickness, as long as the electron blocking characteristics are not compromised.

the performance of such two layer cells can be optimized, but only by considering all the materials electrical properties.
, in order to achieve the highest possible cell performance, the electron blocking layer must be made of a material that exhibits the highest possible electronic conductivity.

a proper design of the cell, in particular of the electron blocking layer thickness, requires knowledge of the materials properties, and in particular the electronic transport properties.
